title: Find the Bug: D Flip-Flop Reset Polarity
statement: A broken D flip-flop module is provided that uses the wrong reset polarity and fails to clear on a high reset signal. Your task is to identify the bug and implement the corrected flip-flop with active-high synchronous reset. The module should behave correctly for all clock and reset combinations.
module_signature: module find_bug_dff_reset_polarity(input clk, input rst, input d, output reg q);
behavior: q captures d on the rising edge when rst is low.
q clears to 0 on the rising edge when rst is high.
The reset is synchronous and active-high.
All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
rst is active-high and synchronous unless the problem statement explicitly says otherwise.
Use non-blocking assignments in clocked always blocks.
Outputs must never depend on uninitialized x/z state after reset.
When rst is asserted on a rising edge, registered outputs reset to their documented initial values.
constraints: Do not use asynchronous reset or implicit level-sensitive constructs.
hint: The bug is the wrong reset polarity in the clocked always block.
